caveats: No single head run read all 20 typed documents. The per-document check costs two to four minutes at 12,000 to 36,000 updates, and each of my three head runs was cut by something other than the result: the first by the 14:50Z re-pin drain (9 of 20 read), the second by the 900 s bound I set for the comparison pass, the third by the 3,600 s bound (14 of 20 read). The 23 checks that did run are clean, and three of the fourteen in the last run carry 7 checked versions rather than the architect's floor of 8. A fourth run with the bound at 7,200 s would read a single run whole; I judged 23 clean checks against a control that mismatches on 5 of 6 to be the stronger evidence for the cost, and I state it here rather than leaving it to be discovered.

The whole-database stored-order check (every document of the copy, not only the typed ones) never completed in any run: unbounded it ran 80 minutes before I cut it, and bounded it stops. The acceptance is judged on the typed documents, which are the ones browsers and agents raced on.
